findings.what: ram_ff91e0 is newly declared short, but its existing cache consumers in graphics/glyph_map.c:1 and player/mole.c:33 declare unsigned short. PreGenerateRandoms only clears the word, so its packet does not establish signedness. No binary defect was observed, but the same cross-unit object has incompatible type claims.
findings.suggested_fix: Use extern unsigned short ram_ff91e0 consistently. The private recommended/random_cache.c does so and matches both revisions; the combined recommended full builds also PASS. Adoption changes prepared source hashes and requires a new immutable checkpoint.

findings.what: The new func_004f50 declaration returns unsigned short, whereas change_level.c:11, level_changes.c:8, and level_generation.c:13 declare unsigned long. The packet narrows a result to a word and zero-extends it into full D0; these callers immediately narrow it, so matching alone does not uniquely establish the historical return-type spelling. The cross-unit inconsistency is directly observed.
findings.suggested_fix: Choose one evidenced return declaration across callers. Minimal demonstrated fix: use the existing extern unsigned long func_004f50() in region_cleanup.c. Both complete cleanup units and the combined recommended full builds MATCH/PASS for both revisions. Alternatively consolidate a different consistent type only after checking all affected callers. Any adoption needs a new prepare/checkpoint.

findings.what: New storage declarations disagree with existing map units: gMapDataD is a bounded [26][19] byte array here versus [52][19] elsewhere, and ELEVATOR_POS_TABLE is char[3][2] here versus struct elevator_position[8] in level_changes.c/change_level.c. Observed accesses agree within the common prefix, and the leading-view comment is candid, but an extern object declaration is not a separate typed view and these are incompatible declarations of the same objects.
findings.suggested_fix: Reuse the established [52][19] byte-grid declaration and struct elevator_position { char x, y; } ELEVATOR_POS_TABLE[8], reading .x/.y for the three tested pairs. Private recommended/region_walk.c and recommended/region_cleanup.c demonstrate that all affected functions still MATCH both revisions and both full ROMs PASS. Prefer a shared declaration when integrating; use a new immutable checkpoint.

findings.what: MapGenerationLookupTables is redeclared with a second record type, struct MapGenerationLookups, rather than the existing struct map_generation_tables in level_generation.c:3-9. Both total 196 bytes and agree at the accessed offsets 16 and 36, but they have different tags, member names, and tail members. This adds another inconsistent cross-unit object type without a matching necessity.
findings.suggested_fix: Reuse the existing map_generation_tables layout and its edge_plain/edge_alternate fields. The complete private recommended/region_cleanup.c and combined recommended full builds prove both revisions remain byte-identical. Consolidate the declaration rather than retaining a second convention; any adoption needs a new prepare/checkpoint.

findings.what: The comments describe runs of four/five without the preserved counter-history qualification. A nonqualifying cell sets run_length to 1 without resetting previous_terrain. A specified sequence of one qualifying label, a gap, then the same label therefore triggers a non-edge action after only three subsequent qualifying cells (or an edge clear after four). Packets confirm the reset behavior; scanner-counter-trace.json records a source-level witness. This is not a claim that the sequence occurs during gameplay or that the original intent is known.
findings.suggested_fix: Clarify the source comments to describe counter thresholds and the preserved remembered-label/reset-to-one quirk; keep executable code unchanged. If it is explicitly characterized as an original bug, label that interpretation and preserve the required ORIGINAL BUG marker. Gameplay reachability and unintended original intent remain [INFERENCE].
